newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Worldwide Semiconductor gets T$15 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Worldwide Semiconductor gets T$15 bln loan.

text.p: Taiwan's Worldwide Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp, an affiliate of Winbond Electronics, has obtained T$15 billion in syndicated loans, lead underwriter China Development said on Friday.
"Several foreign and local banks have decided to conduct the seven-year T$15 billion in syndicated loan to Worldwide Semiconductor," China Development vice-president Grace Fang told Reuters.

China Development is also one of Worldwide Semiconductor's major shareholders. The firm was founded in May 1997 jointly by Winbond, China Development, China Steel and Yulon Motor to produce integrated circuits, Fang said.
A Worldwide Semiconductor spokesman also confirmed that it had obtained the loan.
Fifty-five percent of the loan will be denominated in U.S. dollars at a rate of SIBOR plus 0.7 percentage point, Fang said.

The remaining 45 percent will be conducted in Taiwan dollars, with a loan rate of the state postal funds' one-year timing deposit rate -- currently at 6.05 percent -- plus one percentage point, or 7.05 percent, she said.
The funds will be used to build Worldwide Semiconductor's eight-inch wafer plant, which was expected to start operations in mid-1998, Fang said.
China Development is Taiwan's leading venture capital and investment firm.
